title: Cold-pothole telemetry jot
content:
Context: chasing these weird, short-lived p99 spikes that show up when a previously idle shard receives a small burst (~10-30 concurrent) after a >20s idle. Not the usual cold-start (model load), more like a "pothole" in the execution path where token emission stalls for 30–150ms intermittently.

Notes to self / quick hypothesis:
- Looks related to cold-path in the runtime where KV-cache priming and attention kernel selection happen asynchronously.
- Suspect two contributing factors: (A) transient GC/allocator fragmentation on worker process at first real work after idle; (B) a kernel-selection fallback where optimized kernel misses and we hit a slower fallback for the first few steps.
- Also observed a subtle correlation with background checkpointing (snapshots) on the same host (rare).

Experiment plan (mini-bench harness):
- Model: open-llama-7B-like synthetic (deterministic smaller weights locally so runs are fast).
- Hardware: single A10G-equivalent VM (2x processes pinned) and a multi-tenant test cluster node (4x processes).
- Runtime build: current main + local patch to log kernel-selection path (PR:987).
- Ingress pattern: 3-phase arrival script
  * idle priming: run no traffic for 30s
  * impulse: 12 concurrent 16-token requests sent with Poisson inter-arrival (lambda tuned to produce 12 conns within 150ms)
  * tail: follow with 1 qps for 60s
- Each trial: 100 impulses, 5s between impulses. Collect per-token timing, kernel path logs, allocator pause traces.
- Baseline: run same with continuous small traffic (1 qps sustained) to compare.

Commands / harness snippets:
- injector (local): python tools/impulse_injector.py --concurrency 12 --tokens 16 --poisson --trials 100 --idle 30 --interval 5 --target http://localhost:8080/v1/generate
- server run: make run-debug KERNEL_LOG=1 MALLOC_ARENA=2
- pull logs: scripts/collect-telemetry.sh $TRIAL_ID > /tmp/telemetry-$TRIAL_ID.json

Observed raw numbers (first run, single node):
- baseline (steady 1 qps): p50=18ms p95=34ms p99=48ms throughput steady
- impulse pattern: p50=21ms p95=62ms p99=190ms (outliers at 110–150ms frequent in first token emission)
- outlier distribution by token index: 84% of >100ms events happen on token 1 or 2 of response (strongly suggests priming/kernels)
- kernel-selection log: ~27% of impulses report FALLBACK_KERNEL for attention forward on step 1; subsequent steps switch to OPT_KERN after cache warmup
- allocator traces: small (~2–8ms) pause spikes in some traces concurrent with fallback events, but not all

Quick chart ideas to add to formal notes (sketch here):
- stacked violin: latency distribution by token index (1..16) for impulse vs baseline
- timeline heatmap: per-trial kernel path (OPT vs FALLBACK) aligned to latency spikes
- dot plot: idle-duration (30s, 60s, 120s) vs fraction of FALLBACK_KERNEL events

Interim conclusions:
- Primary vector: kernel-selection fallback at first token. Root cause likely a missing/pre-warmed kernel choice table for that particular sequence length or a heuristic that defers selecting opt kernels until some statistics are gathered.
- Secondary vector: occasional allocator/Glibc arena contention contributes extra jitter and can amplify stalls when fallback occurs concurrently.
- Checkpoint/snapshot activity appears correlated in ~10% of failures on the multi-tenant node; moving snapshots away alleviates a subset.

Immediate mitigations to try (small PRs/ops moves):
1) Force eager kernel path resolution for first token after idle (config flag) — cheap experiment.
2) Warm-up probe (1 short synthetic request) before serving real burst for customers on Dedicated lanes where latency SLOs are strict. Document as "pothole priming" in ops runbook.
3) Reduce MALLOC_ARENA/enable tcmalloc in debug builds for comparison; measure effect on micro-pauses.
4) Ensure snapshotting windows don't overlap with expected busy windows for multi-tenant night runs (ops note).

Longer term (research tickets):
- Rework kernel-selection heuristic to be explicit / stateless so it never falls back to unoptimized path on first emission. Ticket: RDW-3578.
- Add a compact fast-path that guarantees deterministic first-token latency bound (maybe a tiny fused kernel) — feasibility spike needed.

Open questions / TODOs:
- TODO: run same experiment with quantized weights (8-bit) — does fallback probability change? Could be different kernels.
- TODO: replay trial traces through profiler in PR:987 instrumentation and mark exact NPU op mismatch.
- Ask Maya: can we get heap prof traces for the hosts that showed allocator pauses? (Slacked her)
- Verify on different instance types (H100-equivalent) — hardware-specific kernel logic might behave differently.

Rough timeline:
- 11/13: initial sketch + harness (done)
- 11/16: first 3 runs + logs collected (done)
- 11/20: small eject patch to force eager kernel resolution (WIP)
- 12/02: this jot updated with multi-node cross-checks and notes (current)

Notes-to-self (informal):
- When writing up for eng-wide postmortem: emphasize that this is not full cold start; framing as "edge potholes" resonated more with SRE folk.
- Keep the phrase "pothole priming" for ops playbook — short and descriptive.
- If we wire a cheap warm-probe for Dedicated customers, add it behind a config so Hosted can opt-in for low-latency tiers.

Contact: ping Hugo (hugo@redwood.ai) for raw traces. Will move to confluence page once we have distilled charts and a clear remediation strategy.
